body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat d_{\rm sp}=\min_{\theta:\sum_{j=1}^K j^{2\beta}\theta_j^2\le R^2,\ \eta\le\sum_{j=1}^K\theta_jv_j(w)\le1-\eta}\|\widehat b^{\rm te}-\widehat A^{\rm tr}\theta\|_2\)

sampling_model.design: Two equal independent folds of an i.i.d. sample from \(P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}\).
sampling_model.units: Observed triples \(O_i=(X_i,W_i,Y_i)\), with ordered \(K\)-point supports for \(X_i,W_i\) and binary \(Y_i\).
sampling_model.treatment: No randomized treatment is introduced; \(X\) is the exposure index in the observable single-NCO restriction.
sampling_model.overlap: The marginal masses of \(X\) and \(W\) lie between \(\eta/K\) and \(1/(\eta K)\); outcome-specific joint cells may be zero in the upper-bound class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The label-DCT bases are deterministic. The training fold estimates \(G_X\) and \(B\), clips the training Gram spectrum, and forms \(\widehat A^{\rm tr}=\widehat W_X^{\rm tr}\widehat B^{\rm tr}\); the testing fold estimates \(m\) and forms \(\widehat b^{\rm te}=\widehat W_X^{\rm tr}\widehat m^{\rm te}\). Sharp calibration must include the operator, metric, and testing scores together with active-face geometry.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: We derive the asymptotic level and power properties for our tests.
The adaptive test attains the oracle minimax rate within a square-root log-log term in mildly ill-posed models.
We have established optimal separation conditions via a sharp control of the associated minimax separation radius.
We derive nonasymptotic minimax radii for signal detection and goodness of fit with noisy operator observations.
Uniformly valid critical values are obtained through a bootstrap procedure approximating a subset of the local parameter space.
This paper develops a uniformly valid and asymptotically nonconservative test based on projection for shape restrictions.
A coincidence-based test detects nonuniformity from very sparsely sampled discrete data.
The tests are locally minimax-optimal and depend on the known null probabilities.

body.tldr: The proposal directly tests the observed-law null \(d(P)=0\), where \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is a user-chosen smooth bounded diagnostic class and both the support and conditional-expectation operator are learned. A deterministic label-DCT coordinate system makes the split convex program implementable, and a finite-sample projection inequality supplies honest size and a lower confidence bound. For fixed \(K\), the root-\(n\) upper bound is matched by a transverse two-point converse whenever the ambient classes admit designs with one common positive cell, marginal, and link slack over \(a\). Under the explicit DCT compatibility condition, a legal positive-multinomial dense block also gives the \(K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) obstruction when \(K=o(n^{2/3})\) and the worst-case tail condition \(K^{-(a_L+\beta)}\le c_0K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) holds. The complete growing-\(K\) phase diagram and valid adaptation to unknown \(a\) remain open questions.

project_justification.gap: Existing single-NCO diagnostics, inverse-testing results, and convex-projection methods do not give finite-sample uniform testing or a sharp minimax radius for the observed-law null \(d(P)=0\) when a user-chosen bounded source image and its operator are estimated from one growing multinomial table.
project_justification.niche: The observed-image norm makes weak proxies shrink the diagnostic null geometry rather than mechanically amplify noise by inversion. This creates a distinct phase diagram governed by moving convex-set geometry, operator estimation, and legal table perturbations.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a deterministic-coordinate split projection upper bound, a matched fixed-support \(n^{-1/2}\) converse under an explicit ambient common-design premise, and a legal positive-multinomial dense-block lower bound of order \(K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) on the stated compatibility and worst-case-tail subregime. It leaves the operator-nuisance match, active-face calibration, complete phase diagram, adaptation factor, and maximal polynomial \(K\) range as the remaining frontier problems.

body.related_work: Wu, Fu, Wang, Wang, and Sun's Theorem 1 proves existence of a square-integrable single-NCO bridge under their causal-null, NCO, completeness, and Picard hypotheses. Those hypotheses do not imply membership in the user-chosen class \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), and no such implication is used here. Their residual tests motivate the observed-law diagnostic but do not provide the moving-image minimax frontier. Only in an application that separately stipulates that the relevant Wu bridge lies in \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) does rejection conditionally falsify that restricted causal submodel; nonrejection identifies nothing. Breunig and Chen provide the closest adaptive minimax conditional-moment method, but their separation is imposed on an NPIV structural function. Marteau and Sapatinas and Schluttenhofer and Johannes isolate signal and operator noise in diagonal Gaussian sequence experiments and therefore inform, but do not settle, the coupled multinomial problem. Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos regularize local parameter spaces for constrained conditional moments, and Fang and Seo use projection monotonicity for fixed convex cones; the bounded image here is random and nonhomogeneous. Paninski and Chhor and Carpentier provide the legal simplex and local-probability lower-bound technology. The present dense-block result implements a common-null positive-multinomial mixture on an explicit DCT-compatible subregime, while a converse matching all operator-fitting and active-face costs remains unresolved.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A naive held-out residual bootstrap that freezes a training estimate omits training variance: even the scalar equal-split Gaussian analogue has nominal \(5\%\) rejection probability \(2\{1-\Phi(z_{0.975}/\sqrt2)\}=16.58\%\). Moreover, the two-sided input link permits arbitrary legal rotations of output directions, so output-DCT tail smoothness cannot be assumed. These diagnostics constrain the proof architecture and are not theorem claims about any published estimator.
body.honest_scope: The formal null is the observed-law condition \(d(P)=0\); \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is a user-chosen statistical diagnostic class. Wu et al.'s assumptions alone do not place their bridge in this class. Rejection has a causal falsification reading only within applications that separately stipulate this restricted submodel, and nonrejection identifies nothing. The finite-sample split-projection guarantee and lower confidence bound hold over the declared union class. Fixed-support root-\(n\) sharpness additionally uses the explicit premise that the ambient classes admit \( (X,W) \) designs with one common positive cell, marginal, and link slack over \(a\). The legal dense lower bound holds under its displayed DCT compatibility condition, \(K=o(n^{2/3})\), and the uniform worst-case tail condition \(K^{-(a_L+\beta)}\le c_0K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\); here \(a\ge a_L\) transfers that tail control to every \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\). The operator-nuisance converse, complete frontier, sharp active-face calibration, adaptation factor, and maximal polynomial \(K\) range remain open-ended questions.
